method: Full reread of all25 frozen current items and the prior snapshot-validation report, including all clinical content, keys and metadata. Not a hash-only or metadata carry-forward.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

sourceChecks.note: Retrieved current insulin-pen warning that sharing remains unsafe even if needles are changed; no product-specific dosing used.
Retrieved immediate-call advice for sore throat and fever during methimazole.
Subsequently opened full Health Canada safety review: ketoacidosis can occur with normal or modest glucose; respiratory/GI symptoms warrant immediate assessment regardless of glucose.

items.assessment: The urgent teaching misconception is basal omission in type1diabetes during illness. Food choice, mealtime adjustments and recovery activity are relevant but do not correct continuing basal insulin need; sick-day plan avoids arbitrary dosing.
Lipohypertrophy assessment/healthy-site rotation is appropriate. Two alternatives announce their incompleteness with only/without a plan. Make them straightforward competing interventions.
issues: Lipohypertrophy assessment/healthy-site rotation is appropriate. Two alternatives announce their incompleteness with only/without a plan. Make them straightforward competing interventions.

options: Assess injection sites and teach rotation into healthy tissue
Request a higher insulin dose for the persistent high readings
Rotate daily between the abdomen, upper arms and thighs
Teach deeper injections into the same lump
why: Lipohypertrophy can cause unpredictable absorption and needs correction before assuming dose failure.
Increasing insulin before correcting unpredictable absorption can cause hypoglycaemia when injections move into healthy tissue.
Frequent changes between body regions may add absorption variation; a consistent site-rotation plan within suitable healthy tissue is needed.
Changing depth does not restore normal absorption in damaged tissue.

items.assessment: Changing needles does not make a shared insulin pen safe because internal blood contamination is possible. Known infection status, same dose and external cleaning do not resolve the risk; foundation label matches demand.
Device-specific reteaching/return demonstration is sound; the verbal alternative advertises lack of observation. Replace it with a plausible incomplete understanding check.
issues: Device-specific reteaching/return demonstration is sound; the verbal alternative advertises lack of observation. Replace it with a plausible incomplete understanding check.

options: Explain the new pen instructions and ask the client to repeat the prescribed dose
Use the old syringe markings while following the new pen label
Reteach dosing with the prescribed pen and return demonstration
Convert to the old syringe volume using the previous label
why: Repeating the dose checks recall but does not establish the ability to use the unfamiliar concentrated-insulin device correctly.
The syringe markings may not correspond to the concentrated pen product.
Observed device-specific technique helps prevent a concentration-related dosing error.
Old volume instructions may deliver the wrong amount of concentrated insulin.

items.assessment: Current shakiness after missed lunch on gliclazide with a meter available calls for immediate measurement and the supplied low-glucose plan. Rest, routine snack with delayed testing and tomorrow’s regimen change do not assess the present risk.
Dehydration and new AKI change metformin safety even at an unchanged chronic dose. Prompt review before administration avoids accumulation risk; neither food nor an arbitrary half-dose resolves it.
The SGLT2-DKA key is supported despite modest glucose. Remove the explicit missing-ketone cue from the routine glucose-recheck alternative.
issues: The SGLT2-DKA key is supported despite modest glucose. Remove the explicit missing-ketone cue from the routine glucose-recheck alternative.

options: Repeat capillary glucose in one hour to decide whether emergency assessment is needed
Urgently assess for ketones and acid-base disturbance
Use the glucose value to exclude a diabetic emergency
Hydrate while arranging routine sick-day telephone review later
why: Glucose may understate SGLT2-associated ketoacidosis; persistent vomiting, abdominal pain and deep breathing warrant urgent assessment now.
SGLT2-associated ketoacidosis can be serious even when glucose is only moderately elevated.
Moderate glucose does not exclude ketoacidosis with this medication and symptom pattern.
Persistent vomiting and deep breathing require more urgent assessment.

items.assessment: Changed severe persistent pain needs assessment before further semaglutide. Wrong choices use explicit only/without-reporting qualifiers rather than believable routine-intolerance plans.
issues: Changed severe persistent pain needs assessment before further semaglutide. Wrong choices use explicit only/without-reporting qualifiers rather than believable routine-intolerance plans.

options: Use small frequent drinks and judge the response by whether nausea settles
Request a smaller dose at the next routine medication review
Arrange prompt clinical assessment before further dosing
Apply the previous mild-nausea plan and reassess tomorrow
why: Nausea relief does not exclude a serious cause of continuing severe upper-abdominal pain.
A routine dose discussion is too delayed for persistent severe pain with repeated vomiting.
Severe persistent pain differs from earlier mild nausea and requires evaluation.
The changed severity makes routine delayed self-management insufficient.

items.assessment: New hyperglycaemia after prednisone can be medication related without proving permanent diabetes. Prior normal values or thirst alone do not authorize independent steroid reduction; key accurately frames increased monitoring need.

Dose return demonstration and low-glucose response knowledge support independent insulin use. Agreement without demonstration, cap-colour identification and unavailable assistance do not establish readiness.
Prolonged prednisone requires individualized discontinuation review. Option0 expressly advertises no review; use inappropriate reuse of a prior short-course plan.
issues: Prolonged prednisone requires individualized discontinuation review. Option0 expressly advertises no review; use inappropriate reuse of a prior short-course plan.

options: Reuse the taper schedule provided for a previous brief course of prednisone
Arrange a prescriber-directed taper and discuss adrenal suppression
Stop when the current package is finished regardless of dose
Alternate full doses and no doses based on daily symptoms
why: A schedule for a brief course may not account for months of adrenal suppression or the current underlying disease.
Prolonged therapy can suppress endogenous cortisol, making abrupt withdrawal hazardous.
Package completion does not establish a safe discontinuation schedule.
An improvised schedule does not address adrenal recovery reliably.

items.assessment: Consistent levothyroxine timing and separation from iron address variable absorption. Higher dose before correcting technique, varying food exposure and separation only on blood-test days do not; foundation label is appropriate.
Adrenergic symptoms after levothyroxine escalation justify thyroid/cardiovascular review. Remove the explicit nonreporting cue from the timing distractor.
issues: Adrenergic symptoms after levothyroxine escalation justify thyroid/cardiovascular review. Remove the explicit nonreporting cue from the timing distractor.

options: Move the levothyroxine dose to bedtime to reduce daytime symptoms
Reassure that symptoms reflect adjustment and keep routine follow-up
Provide relaxation teaching and defer thyroid review unless anxiety persists
Report symptoms for thyroid and cardiovascular assessment
why: Timing changes do not evaluate or correct possible excessive hormone exposure after a dose increase.
The adrenergic symptom cluster after a dose increase warrants earlier review.
Relaxation alone does not address possible excessive hormone replacement.
The temporal pattern suggests possible overreplacement requiring review.

items.assessment: Fever/sore throat on methimazole correctly require prompt team assessment for marrow toxicity. The thyroid-monitoring alternative declares that the fever is ignored; replace with a plausible misplaced monitoring focus.
issues: Fever/sore throat on methimazole correctly require prompt team assessment for marrow toxicity. The thyroid-monitoring alternative declares that the fever is ignored; replace with a plausible misplaced monitoring focus.

options: Promptly contact the treatment team for assessment and blood-count guidance
Use cold remedies and report only if symptoms persist a week
Arrange a thyroid-function test and use its result to decide about review
Treat it as an allergy solely because fever followed treatment
why: Agranulocytosis is uncommon but serious and must be considered.
Delayed assessment may miss a serious drug-associated infection risk.
Thyroid hormone control does not assess neutrophil suppression or infection risk; these symptoms need prompt review and blood-count guidance.
Fever and sore throat require evaluation rather than an assumed mechanism.

items.assessment: Inability to remain upright changes oral alendronate suitability because of oesophageal injury risk. Crushing, food or bedtime administration do not replace positioning requirements; clarification is appropriate.

Excess water intake with reduced urine, weight gain and confusion during desmopressin supports retention/hyponatraemia rather than osmotic loss or inadequate ADH effect. Parallel interpretations use the supplied trajectory.

Vomiting prevents oral hydrocortisone absorption during increased illness demand in adrenal insufficiency. Urgent emergency replacement planning is appropriate; food trials, routine waiting or salt/water alone cannot replace glucocorticoids.

Monitoring during and after exercise plus readily available rapid carbohydrate addresses immediate and delayed lows. A meal does not guarantee protection, symptoms should not be exercised through, and basal omission risks deficiency.
The individualized time-zone plan and accessible supplies are correct. The wrong timing/dosing choices explicitly advertise omitted assessment with without/only.
issues: The individualized time-zone plan and accessible supplies are correct. The wrong timing/dosing choices explicitly advertise omitted assessment with without/only.

options: Keep basal and mealtime doses on the home clock throughout the trip
Pack all insulin with ice directly against the cartridges
Adjust mealtime doses after arrival according to appetite at each meal
Obtain an individualized dosing and monitoring schedule
Carry accessible supplies and hypoglycemia treatment
why: Maintaining every home-clock dose may mismatch changed meal times and dose intervals; an individualized travel plan is needed.
Freezing can damage insulin and make it unreliable.
Appetite alone does not establish carbohydrate intake, glucose status or the appropriate dose intervals across time zones.
Time changes can alter intervals between doses and meals.
Lost checked luggage should not interrupt essential treatment.

items.assessment: Prescribed glucagon rescue plus emergency help and continued assessment is appropriate for severe hypoglycaemia. Unsafe swallowing, partly discharging a single-use device and abandoning monitoring after arousal are meaningful rescue misconceptions.

Unexpected particles in normally clear insulin after heat exposure call for replacement. A normal glucose value cannot verify potency, and recooling or dose compensation cannot reliably reverse unknown damage.

Pump interruption with rising glucose can progress to insulin deficiency before symptoms. Directed glucose/ketone checks and the backup plan are appropriate; an unverified malfunctioning delivery path cannot be assumed to deliver a correction.

Falling tachycardia/tremor without hypothyroid features supports balanced response. Infection warning symptoms, excessive suppression and anxiety improvement without physiological change do not establish the intended benefit.
The unlisted correction-scale range requires authorized escalation. The alternative explicitly says it will leave the result unreported; use a plausible timing error.
issues: The unlisted correction-scale range requires authorized escalation. The alternative explicitly says it will leave the result unreported; use a plausible timing error.

options: Use the highest listed dose as the final plan
Repeat the glucose after the meal before contacting the prescriber
Contact the authorized prescriber or follow the escalation instruction
Extend the scale by repeating its last numerical increment
why: That dose may be insufficient or inappropriate for the unlisted range.
A later value does not replace current clarification of a result outside the authorized dosing scale.
The incomplete scale does not authorize extrapolation to an unlisted range.
A pattern in listed doses is not a prescription for higher values.

items.assessment: New infection symptoms and melena/light-headedness require prompt assessment during chronic steroids, unlike improved mobility or mild isolated appetite/sleep changes. The prompt distinguishes urgent assessment from routine review rather than asserting mild effects are never reportable.
